name: MS Teams Helpdesk Impersonation / Vishing
description: Threat actors abuse Microsoft Teams' default-enabled external access and Quick Assist to impersonate internal IT/helpdesk staff, often after first 'email-bombing' a target's inbox with hundreds of subscription/spam emails to manufacture urgency. The attacker then messages or calls the victim over Teams offering to 'fix' the spam problem, walking them through granting remote control or running a 'patch' that is actually a malware loader. This pattern, pioneered by groups like Storm-1811 and refined by UNC6692 (now deploying the custom 'SNOW' malware suite per Microsoft's April 2026 disclosure), has become a leading human-operated intrusion vector because users trust internal collaboration-platform messages far more than email. Microsoft's April 2026 'cross-tenant helpdesk impersonation' playbook and multiple CSO/TheHackerNews reports confirm the technique is now being used against financial institutions in a documented 9-stage attack chain leading to data exfiltration and ransomware staging.

mitre_techniques.notes: Cross-tenant Microsoft Teams messages used to directly contact targets while posing as IT support
Pre-attack email-bombing campaign floods the inbox with subscription spam to create urgency
Victim is talked into downloading and running a 'fix' or 'patch' that is the malware payload
Victim is guided to install or accept Quick Assist / RMM session, giving the attacker hands-on-keyboard access
Captured credentials and approved MFA prompts are reused for follow-on access
Attacker triggers MFA prompts during the call and instructs the victim to approve them

notable_examples: Microsoft's April 2026 'Cross-tenant helpdesk impersonation to data exfiltration' blog detailing a human-operated intrusion playbook abusing Teams external access
UNC6692 campaign deploying the custom 'SNOW' malware suite (including a malicious browser extension) after Teams-based helpdesk impersonation, per TheHackerNews April 2026 reporting
9-stage attack chain documented against financial institutions combining email-bombing, Teams vishing, and remote access tool installation
CSO Online and Field Effect reporting on enterprise intrusions where attackers initiate unsolicited Teams calls offering to resolve a 'spam filter' or 'security update' issue
Continued evolution from the 2024 Storm-1811 Quick Assist campaigns into broader cross-tenant Teams impersonation by multiple criminal crews in 2025-2026
detection_opportunities: Alert on inbound Teams chats/calls from external (cross-tenant) accounts with display names containing 'Help Desk', 'IT Support', 'Service Desk', etc.
Restrict or disable Microsoft Teams External Access tenant-wide, or allowlist only known partner tenants
Correlate sudden spikes in inbound mailbox volume (email-bombing) with subsequent external Teams contact to the same user within a short window
Block or tightly govern Quick Assist and other unmanaged remote-support tools via application control policies
Monitor for new MFA device/method enrollments occurring shortly after an external Teams session
Hunt for process execution of remote admin tooling or browser extension installs immediately following a Teams screen-share/remote-control session
Train users to verify all 'IT support' contact through a known internal ticketing channel, never via unsolicited Teams messages
